#region VEXcode Generated Robot Configuration
from vex import *
import urandom
import math

# Brain should be defined by default
brain=Brain()

# Robot configuration code
left_drive_smart = Motor(Ports.PORT1, GearSetting.RATIO_18_1, False)
right_drive_smart = Motor(Ports.PORT2, GearSetting.RATIO_18_1, True)
drivetrain = DriveTrain(left_drive_smart, right_drive_smart, 319.19, 295, 40, MM, 1)
distance_3 = Distance(Ports.PORT3)


# wait for rotation sensor to fully initialize
wait(30, MSEC)


# Make random actually random
def initializeRandomSeed():
    wait(100, MSEC)
    random = brain.battery.voltage(MV) + brain.battery.current(CurrentUnits.AMP) * 100 + brain.timer.system_high_res()
    urandom.seed(int(random))
      
# Set random seed 
initializeRandomSeed()


def play_vexcode_sound(sound_name):
    # Helper to make playing sounds from the V5 in VEXcode easier and
    # keeps the code cleaner by making it clear what is happening.
    print("VEXPlaySound:" + sound_name)
    wait(5, MSEC)

# add a small delay to make sure we don't print in the middle of the REPL header
wait(200, MSEC)
# clear the console to make sure we don't have the REPL in the console
print("\033[2J")

#endregion VEXcode Generated Robot Configuration

# Library imports
from vex import *

# Begin project code

# Variables

noCollision = True #sets the initial loop state
distance_sensor = Distance(Ports.PORT3) #construct distance sensor
pmeter = PotentiometerV2(brain.three_wire_port.a) #construct all meters and switches
bswitch = Bumper(brain.three_wire_port.b)
lswitch = Limit(brain.three_wire_port.c)
# Functions
def checkDistance(): #function for less repeated code
    currentDistance = distance_sensor.object_distance(MM) #gets the current distance away from object
    wait(30, MSEC)
    if currentDistance <= 200:
        global noCollision #use global to modify the first variable
        noCollision = False #we are too close, stop the loop
        drivetrain.stop() #stop the motors
        wait(1, SECONDS)
    else: 
        drivetrain.drive(FORWARD) #if not close, move forward for a second
        wait(1, SECONDS)
        drivetrain.stop() #stop to check again
def printScreen(): #function for printing values of all switches and meters
    brain.screen.clear_screen() #clear previous values
    brain.screen.set_cursor(1,1) #set cursor to first position
    brain.screen.print("Potentiometer: " + str(pmeter.angle(PERCENT))) #print the value of the potentiometer
    brain.screen.set_cursor(2, 1) #set cursor to second pos
    brain.screen.print("Bump Switch: " + str(bswitch.pressing())) #print value
    brain.screen.set_cursor(3,1) #set to third pos
    brain.screen.print("Limit Switch: " + str(lswitch.pressing())) #print value
    brain.screen.set_cursor(4,1) #set to fourth pos
    brain.screen.print("Distance: " + str(distance_sensor.object_distance(MM)) #print current distance
# Body of code
drivetrain.set_drive_velocity(10, PERCENT) #set initial speed 
onoff = -1 #PLTW requirement for turning on motors
while (True): #infinite loop
    printScreen() #call print function
    distance = distance_sensor.object_distance(MM)
    angle = pmeter.angle(PERCENT) #set the variable for the potentiometer's value
    wait(50,MSEC) #PLTW requirement for correctly printing
    drivetrain.set_drive_velocity(angle, PERCENT) #set the motors velocity whatever value potentiometer is at
    if (bswitch.pressing() != 0 and lswitch.pressing() != 0): #check for both switches being on
        onoff = 1 #set value of should spin motors or not
    else:
        onoff = -1 #if we do -onoff, it could be -1 going to 1 so absolute is better

    if (onoff == 1): #if we want the motor to move then execute this code
        if (distance <= 300): #check if we are close to the other group
            if (angle < 10): #if the value of potentiometer is less than 10 percent, we probably don't want it to move, so don't move still
                drivetrain.stop() #stops it if moving
            else:
                drivetrain.drive(FORWARD) #we want to stop after X amount and break the loops.
                wait(1,SECONDS)
                drivetrain.stop()
                break
    else:
        drivetrain.stop() #stop if onoff is false
        else: #runs if we aren't close enough
            if (angle < 10): #same as above
                drivetrain.stop() #same as above
            else:
                drivetrain.drive(FORWARD) #keep driving as we aren't close enough
    wait(300, MSEC) #wait before checking again
